# Introduction

This vignette runs a small, self-contained **MurineMatchTx** workflow using
synthetic data. Every code chunk executes with the installed package; no download
or separately distributed example archive is needed. The examples verify
software behavior only. They are not biological validation, cross-species
validation, or evidence that any mouse model represents human disease.

PCA is a QC and structure diagnostic. DEG concordance and TROM describe distinct
aspects of the supplied data; they are not combined with PCA, GO, TME, or
metabolism into a model-selection total score.

# Synthetic expression and explicit sample metadata

The four samples and 200 shared gene labels below are invented. In real use,
prepare a common, audited ortholog feature space before merging expression
tables. `prepare_PCA_data()` merges matching gene labels; it does not establish
orthology. These continuous values represent an already transformed expression
scale for PCA and TROM, not raw counts or TPM.

```{r synthetic-expression}
work_dir <- tempfile("MurineMatchTx-vignette-")
dir.create(work_dir)
sample_ids <- c("human_tumor", "human_normal", "mouse_normal", "mouse_tumor")
expression <- matrix(
  rnorm(200 * 4), nrow = 200,
  dimnames = list(paste0("gene", seq_len(200)), sample_ids)
)
sample_metadata <- data.frame(
  sample_id = sample_ids,
  species = c("human", "human", "mouse", "mouse"),
  dataset = c("HumanDemo", "HumanDemo", "MouseDemo", "MouseDemo"),
  model = c("Reference", "Reference", "ModelA", "ModelA"),
  tissue = c("tumor", "normal", "normal", "tumor")
)
human_expression_file <- file.path(work_dir, "human.csv")
mouse_expression_file <- file.path(work_dir, "mouse.csv")
write.csv(data.frame(X = rownames(expression), expression[, 1:2]),
          human_expression_file, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.frame(X = rownames(expression), expression[, 3:4]),
          mouse_expression_file, row.names = FALSE)
sample_metadata
```

# PCA first: uncorrected structure

Metadata are deliberately shuffled to demonstrate the join by `sample_id`.
The default retains uncorrected data and records the choice. Here base R draws
the four points without attempting group ellipses from one sample per group.
For larger datasets, `plot_PCA_tinyarray()` accepts the same `pca_data` object.

```{r pca-qc}
pca_data <- prepare_PCA_data(
  human_expression_file,
  list(ModelA = mouse_expression_file),
  sample_metadata = sample_metadata[c(4, 2, 1, 3), ]
)
stopifnot(
  identical(pca_data$sample_metadata$sample_id, colnames(pca_data$merged_data)),
  identical(pca_data$merged_data, pca_data$uncorrected_data),
  identical(pca_data$parameters$batch_correction, FALSE),
  is.null(pca_data$corrected_data)
)
pca <- prcomp(t(as.matrix(pca_data$uncorrected_data)), center = TRUE)
plot(pca$x[, 1:2], pch = 19, xlab = "PC1", ylab = "PC2",
     main = "Synthetic expression: QC only")
text(pca$x[, 1:2], labels = rownames(pca$x), pos = 3, cex = 0.7)
pca_data$parameters
```

ComBat requires an explicit `batch_correction = TRUE`. When species and dataset
are completely confounded, it may remove biological species differences and the
package warns about that limitation. Corrected output carries a provenance
attribute and cannot be used as raw count or TPM input.

# DEG formats and shared thresholds

The next files mimic edgeR and DESeq2 output columns. `deg_method = "limma"`
uses `logFC` and `adj.P.Val`; custom formats require explicit column mappings.
The human contrast is called `TCGA` by the DEG interface even though all values
here are synthetic. Fold-change cutoffs are inclusive and FDR cutoffs exclusive:
an FDR of exactly 0.05 is stable under these thresholds.

```{r deg-inputs}
thresholds <- list(log2fc = 1, fdr = 0.05)
human_ids <- paste0("ENSG00000", seq_len(4))
mouse_ids <- paste0("ENSMUSG00000", seq_len(4))
human_deg <- data.frame(
  gene = human_ids, logFC = c(1, -1, 2, 0.5),
  FDR = c(0.01, 0.01, 0.05, 0.01)
)
mouse_deg <- data.frame(
  gene = mouse_ids, log2FoldChange = c(1.2, -1.5, 2, -0.5),
  padj = c(0.02, 0.02, 0.01, 0.2)
)
human_deg_file <- file.path(work_dir, "human_deg.csv")
mouse_deg_file <- file.path(work_dir, "mouse_deg.csv")
write.csv(human_deg, human_deg_file, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(mouse_deg, mouse_deg_file, row.names = FALSE)
mouse_files <- list(ModelA = mouse_deg_file)
methods <- c(TCGA = "edgeR", ModelA = "DESeq2")
merged_DEG <- merge_DEG_datasets(
  human_deg_file, mouse_files, deg_method = methods,
  gene_col = "gene", deg_thresholds = thresholds
)
stopifnot(identical(
  merged_DEG$change[merged_DEG$contrast == "TCGA"],
  c("Up", "Down", "Stable", "Stable")
))
merged_DEG
```

```{r deg-volcano}
deg_output <- paste0(file.path(work_dir, "deg"), "/")
dir.create(deg_output)
volcano <- plot_DEG_volcano(merged_DEG, output_path = deg_output)
print(volcano)
```

# Audited mapping, DEG heatmap and barplot

The mapping below is a **fabricated contract fixture**, not a Compara export.
Its `release` label explicitly records that origin. Real analyses need the
actual mapping release and high-confidence one-to-one relationships; ambiguous
and low-confidence pairs are excluded and the audit records their removal.

```{r deg-mapping-and-plots}
ortholog_map <- data.frame(
  human_gene_id = human_ids,
  mouse_gene_id = mouse_ids,
  human_gene_id_version = paste0(human_ids, ".1"),
  mouse_gene_id_version = paste0(mouse_ids, ".1"),
  homology_type = "ortholog_one2one",
  is_high_confidence = TRUE,
  release = "synthetic-software-example"
)
heatmap_input <- prepare_DEG_heatmap_data(
  human_deg_file, mouse_files, deg_method = methods, gene_col = "gene",
  deg_thresholds = thresholds, ortholog_map = ortholog_map
)
heatmap_input$mapping_audit
merge_edger <- plot_DEG_heatmap(
  heatmap_input, mouse_files, output_path = deg_output
)
stopifnot(
  identical(rownames(merge_edger), human_ids[1:2]),
  identical(as.numeric(merge_edger[, "ModelA"]), c(1, -1)),
  identical(attr(merge_edger, "deg_thresholds"), thresholds)
)
print(plot_DEG_barplot(merge_edger, output_path = deg_output))
```

# TROM and a reference with no normal samples

TROM uses explicit species and tissue metadata. Clinical/CNV annotations are
optional, so they are omitted here. Tissue-mismatched entries are `NA`. To
demonstrate the zero-normal branch, the second call explicitly marks both
invented human samples as tumor; this is a software exercise, not a procedure
for relabelling real samples.

```{r trom}
similarity <- compute_similarity_matrix(
  as.matrix(pca_data$merged_data), sample_metadata = sample_metadata
)
stopifnot(is.na(
  similarity$filtered_similarity_matrix["human_tumor", "mouse_normal"]
))
similarity$filtered_similarity_matrix

tumor_reference_metadata <- sample_metadata
tumor_reference_metadata$tissue[tumor_reference_metadata$species == "human"] <- "tumor"
tumor_similarity <- compute_similarity_matrix(
  as.matrix(pca_data$merged_data), sample_metadata = tumor_reference_metadata
)
trom_file <- file.path(work_dir, "trom.pdf")
heatmap_res <- plot_TROMscore_heatmap(
  dm_trom_del_backgroud_clinic = tumor_similarity$dm_trom_del_backgroud_clinic,
  trom_matrix = tumor_similarity$similarity_matrix,
  sample_metadata = tumor_reference_metadata,
  output_path = trom_file
)
stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(heatmap_res$plot_matrix), "mouse_tumor"),
  all(as.character(heatmap_res$merge_long$group) == "tumor"),
  file.exists(trom_file)
)
heatmap_res$merge_long
```

# Count/TPM provenance and the TME boundary

Raw counts must be finite, non-negative whole numbers. TPM must be finite and
non-negative. External data must declare `input_source`; the label documents
provenance rather than proving it from the numbers. Do not relabel transformed
or ComBat-corrected values as counts or TPM.

This small matrix uses eight real gene symbols solely to exercise the bundled
metabolism signatures. TPM is calculated from invented counts and invented
gene lengths, with each sample summing to one million. Because this conversion
is performed outside the package's TME workflow, its source is `provided_tpm`.

```{r count-and-tpm}
counts <- matrix(
  c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80,
    25, 12, 44, 35, 61, 52, 83, 76,
    40, 30, 20, 10, 80, 70, 60, 50,
    35, 44, 12, 25, 76, 83, 52, 61),
  nrow = 8,
  dimnames = list(
    c("HK1", "LDHA", "PFKM", "ENO1", "NDUFA1", "COX4I1", "ATP5F1A", "ATP5F1B"),
    sample_ids
  )
)
gene_length_kb <- c(1, 2, 1.5, 2.5, 1, 2, 1.5, 2.5)
rates <- sweep(counts, 1, gene_length_kb, "/")
provided_tpm <- sweep(rates, 2, colSums(rates), "/") * 1e6
stopifnot(all(counts >= 0), all(counts == round(counts)),
          all(is.finite(provided_tpm)), all(provided_tpm >= 0),
          all(abs(colSums(provided_tpm) - 1e6) < 1e-8))
tme_inputs <- list(
  data_matrix = provided_tpm,
  input_type = "TPM",
  input_source = "provided_tpm",
  method = "cibersort",
  group_as = unname(pca_data$group_all)
)
stopifnot(length(tme_inputs$group_as) == ncol(tme_inputs$data_matrix))
names(tme_inputs)
```

`tme_inputs` describes the input contract, not a deconvolution result. TME
deconvolution is deliberately outside this offline example: eight genes cannot
support meaningful immune composition estimates. With suitable real data,
`plot_TME_barplot()` returns `eset_tpm`, `method_model`, and `input_metadata`;
`plot_TME_boxplot()` instead takes a TPM data frame, group labels, and a
condition list, and runs CIBERSORT again. Neither deconvolution is run here.

When current human-reference deconvolution signatures are applied to mouse
samples, TME results are exploratory, method-specific descriptions. They do not
enter cross-species similarity scoring or model-selection decisions and do not
establish cross-species validation without mouse-specific signatures or
orthogonal immune evidence.

# GO: define the input boundary

The GO interface needs species-matched **gene symbols** and annotation data.
The invented Ensembl-like IDs above are not valid annotation keys. We can
execute the shared threshold selection and inspect the candidate IDs, but
cannot infer biological enrichment from them. `GO_enrichment_analysis()` also
requires at least two enriched GO terms for its similarity plot. This vignette
does not run enrichment or load an annotation database to manufacture a result.

```{r go-input-boundary}
go_candidates <- subset(merged_DEG, contrast == "TCGA" & change != "Stable")
stopifnot(identical(go_candidates$gene, human_ids[1:2]))
go_contract <- data.frame(
  species = "hsa", org_db = "org.Hs.eg.db", ontology = "BP",
  required_identifiers = "human gene symbols",
  candidates_in_fixture = nrow(go_candidates),
  biological_annotation_available = FALSE
)
go_contract
```

# Offline metabolism scoring

The local `zscore` path uses bundled signatures and does not run TME
deconvolution. A one-gene minimum is used only to exercise the software on this
tiny fixture; it is not a recommended analysis threshold. These synthetic
scores have no metabolic interpretation.

```{r metabolism}
sig_meta <- calculate_metabolism_score(
  provided_tpm, method = "zscore", mini_gene_count = 1,
  input_source = "provided_tpm"
)
stopifnot(
  is.data.frame(sig_meta), setequal(sig_meta$ID, sample_ids),
  identical(attr(sig_meta, "MurineMatchTx_tpm_source"), "provided_tpm")
)
sig_meta
score_groups <- sample_metadata$species[match(sig_meta$ID, sample_metadata$sample_id)]
metabolism_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "metabolism")
metabolism_heatmap <- plot_metabolism_heatmap(
  sig_meta, group_as = score_groups, output_path = metabolism_dir, height = 6
)
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(metabolism_dir, "heatmap.pdf")))
```

When current human-reference metabolism signatures are applied to mouse samples,
scores are exploratory, method-specific descriptions. They do not enter
cross-species similarity scoring or model-selection decisions and do not
establish cross-species validation without mouse-specific signatures or
orthogonal metabolic evidence.

# Generated files

All example inputs and saved plots are written to a new R temporary directory.
The files verify that the plotting functions ran; the printed tables and plots
above remain part of this vignette. No study data or project files are modified.

```{r generated-files}
expected_plots <- c(
  file.path(deg_output, c("volcano_plot.pdf", "heatmap.pdf", "barplot.pdf")),
  trom_file, file.path(metabolism_dir, "heatmap.pdf")
)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(expected_plots)))
list.files(work_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```
